date_note: Reported as happening on Thursday 26 November; the page gives no earlier day.
title: EasyEquities suspends client access after cybersecurity incident
summary: EasyEquities, owned by JSE-listed Purple Group, suspended client access on Thursday after a cybersecurity incident. TechCentral reports the company says a small number of client accounts were specifically targeted, it has not said how many, and that all client funds are accounted for and secure on its investigation so far. Purple Group said it was still establishing whether personal information was accessed.
plain: EasyEquities has paused client access after a cybersecurity incident. The company says a small number of client accounts were targeted and that client funds are accounted for and secure so far; it has not said what information was exposed.
exec: Clients cannot use the platform for now; the company says a small number of accounts were targeted and it is still establishing whether personal information was accessed.
action: EasyEquities asks clients not to log in until it confirms by email and social media that access is restored, and not to share passwords or one-time codes with anyone claiming to be from the platform.

validation.note: The Citizen (republishing Moneyweb) and TechCentral are separate publishers, each stating that EasyEquities suspended access after a cybersecurity incident. The Moneyweb page itself was not read.
